newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Barbara Mines says Deans remains ceo.
newsitem.headline: St Barbara Mines says Deans remains ceo.

text.p: St Barbara Mines Ltd said on Tuesday that an earlier announcement made by one of its directors, Ross Atkins, stating that chief executive Robin Deans no longer held that position was incorrect.

The Atkins announcement said Dean resigned on April 3, because he could not work effectively with Atkins after Atkins was re-elected to the board of St Barbara at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on April 3.
St Barbara said the announcement was not authorised by the company and no prior notice of the announcement was given to the company, its directors or management.
The company said the Atkins announcement misstated the situation and that Dean and the company secretary, Neil Roberts were continuing in their positions.

"The board of St Barbara Mines prior to the EGM accepted the resignations (of Dean and Roberts) and simultaneously offered employment in the event that Peter Jones, Norman Bevan and Leslie Nixon were not removed from the board of directors at the EGM," the company said in its statement.
St Barbara said Dean and Roberts accepted the offer to resume their positions at the conclusion of the EGM.
The company said Atkins' contention that Dean and Roberts were offered re-employment after the EGM pursuant to an invalid resolution was wrong.

Atkins, who jointly controls 47.2 percent of St Barbara with former chairman Alan Birchmore, opposes St Barbara's takeover offer for Mt Leyshon Mines Ltd MLG.AX of 32 St Barbara shares for every 10 Mt Leyshon Mines.
Mt Leyshon has advised shareholders to reject the bid.
At 2.20 p.m (0420 GMT) St Barbara Mines shares were steady at 62 cents, while Mt Leyshon's shares last traded at A$1.96 on Monday.
